page: Microsoft Azure D64_v3 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by the Intel Xeon E5-2673 v4 processor, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 64 vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The instance is equipped with 256 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4 GB of RAM per vCPU. It also includes 1638 GB of local SSD storage, managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark results indicate that the D64_v3 delivers average multi-core performance, as evidenced by its stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores. However, its single-core performance is relatively weak, falling into the bottom 25% in both stress-ng and Geekbench single-core tests. Memory bandwidth remains stable in the average tier, with read-only cached small block speeds reaching 2437.57 GB/sec and uncached large block speeds at 118.68 GB/sec. For specialized tasks, the server handles multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and static web serving at average throughput levels, but exhibits poor performance in LLM text generation, making it unsuitable for modern generative AI workloads.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D64_v3 offers a mature hardware profile with a high density of legacy vCPUs and a substantial local SSD allocation. This makes it a practical choice for workloads that benefit from parallel execution rather than raw single-thread speed. Appropriate workloads include general-purpose web serving, database operations, multi-threaded data processing, and legacy enterprise applications that require a balanced ratio of compute, memory, and local storage without the premium cost of newer-generation architectures.
description: The Microsoft Azure D64_v3 is a general-purpose virtual machine configured with 64 vCPUs and 256 GB of RAM, running on an Intel Xeon E5-2673 v4 processor with x86_64 architecture. Operating under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance features 32 physical cores with hyper-threading and includes 1638 GB of local SSD storage. Benchmark data positions the server's multi-core compute, memory bandwidth, and database operations in the average tier, while its single-core performance is relatively weak. Lacking GPU acceleration, it is not suited for intensive AI text generation. Instead, the D64_v3 provides a resource-dense, cost-effective profile for parallelized legacy workloads, multi-threaded data processing, static web serving, and medium-sized database deployments requiring balanced compute and local storage.
